articles.originalTitle: ENR 2026 Top 100 Green Design Firms and Contractors: Green Building Market Deepens - Engineering News-Record
articles.title: Costs and Sustainability Criteria Examined in the Green Building Market
articles.excerpt: While revenues in green building design and contracting rise, sector participants discuss how cost pressures, labor limits, and shifting federal incentives impact projects.
articles.content: Interest in sustainability practices within the engineering and construction sector continues, while revenues in green design and contracting rose last year. Design firm revenues increased, and contractor revenue experienced similar growth. Certain markets saw increased demand, while other sectors recorded declines. Costs, procurement timelines, and labor resources remain significant factors in project development. Experts note that certifications alone are insufficient, emphasizing that actual building performance and operational efficiency must be prioritized. Highlighting the importance of early coordination, industry representatives state that collaboration between designers and contractors during early project phases improves practical execution. Meanwhile, federal-level incentive and policy changes have created varied effects on projects, with some investors altering approaches due to rising costs and grid reliability concerns. These challenges encountered in design and construction processes require projects to be managed with careful attention to budget and scheduling balance.

articles.originalTitle: The 90s: Art and Fashion - tate.org.uk
articles.title: Tate Britain Explores the Art, Fashion, and Counterculture of the 1990s
articles.excerpt: Curated by Edward Enninful, a new exhibition at Tate Britain brings together photography, fashion, and art to examine a decade that transformed British culture.
articles.content: Tate Britain is presenting The 90s: Art and Fashion, an exhibition exploring a decade defined by bold creativity and a rebellious spirit. Drawing on curator Edward Enninful OBE's experience, the exhibition brings together photography, fashion, art, and design to examine a moment when a new generation transformed British culture. Visitors can encounter iconic works by artists and photographers including Steve McQueen, Sarah Lucas, Yinka Shonibare, Corinne Day, and Juergen Teller, alongside fashion designs by Vivienne Westwood, Alexander McQueen, and John Galliano. The exhibition highlights the lasting influence of a decade that broke down boundaries between art, fashion, and popular culture. Key highlights include Mark Leckey's video work tracing British dance music culture, a tartan look from Vivienne Westwood's autumn/winter 1993 collection Anglomania, Yinka Shonibare's reimagined sculpture The Swing, and Jim Lambie's site-specific floor installation Zobop. Steve McQueen's silent film Bear is also featured. The exhibition runs from 8 October 2026 to 14 February 2027 at Tate Britain, with tickets currently available for booking.

articles.originalTitle: Art Basel announces 272 exhibitors and a reconfigured showfloor for its 2026 Miami Beach edition - Art Basel
articles.title: Art Basel Announces 272 Exhibitors and Reconfigured Showfloor for 2026 Miami Beach Edition

articles.content: Art Basel Miami Beach has announced its exhibitor lineup and reconfigured layout for its 2026 edition, taking place at the Miami Beach Convention Center from December 4 to 6, with VIP previews on December 2 and 3. The fair will bring together 272 exhibitors from more than 40 countries and territories. articles.originalTitle: Tarek Atoui’s Echo Chamber - ArtReview
articles.title: Sound Artist Tarek Atoui Prepares for Turbine Hall Commission
articles.excerpt: Lebanese sound artist and electroacoustic composer Tarek Atoui is developing his largest work to date for Tate Modern's Turbine Hall.
articles.content: Lebanese sound artist and electroacoustic composer Tarek Atoui creates sonic environments in his Paris studio that combine instruments, digital processes, and human collaboration. Atoui is currently developing his largest work to date: the Hyundai Commission for Tate Modern's Turbine Hall, scheduled to open in October. Utilizing the acoustic reverberation of the expansive steel-and-concrete hall, he marks the first sound artist and composer to undertake the commission series. Approaching listening as an active process that enhances environmental understanding, Atoui has developed instruments in collaboration with d/Deaf individuals since 2012, exploring vibration as a tactile phenomenon. His artistic practice draws on improvisation, integrating influences from John Cage, free jazz, and traditional Lebanese music within established architectural parameters.

articles.originalTitle: Brooklyn Museum’s $48m energy-efficiency retrofit is latest in New York City’s effort to cut emissions - The Art Newspaper
articles.title: Brooklyn Museum Undertakes $48m Energy-Efficiency Retrofit Project
articles.excerpt: As part of New York City's efforts to curb emissions, the Brooklyn Museum has launched a $48m energy overhaul to modernize its century-old infrastructure.
articles.content: In line with New York City's efforts to make cultural institutions energy efficient and less dependent on fossil fuels, the Brooklyn Museum is undertaking a $48m infrastructure overhaul. Announced by the Department of Citywide Administrative Services, the Brooklyn Museum and the New York Power Authority, the initiative combines renewable-energy generation with the modernization of museum systems. Expected to be completed in mid-2027, the project aims to reduce carbon emissions. The Deep Energy Retrofit programme includes solar carport panels, a new building-management system and heating, ventilation and air-conditioning upgrades. The museum's ageing steam-generation plant will be replaced with a high-efficiency hot-water system, while electric humidification control will regulate gallery conditions. Hardat Raywat, the museum's deputy director for operations, engineering and facilities, stated that the project is expected to yield roughly a 57% reduction in carbon emissions, amounting to over 3,300 metric tons per year. Brian Chang, deputy commissioner for energy management at the Department of Citywide Administrative Services, noted that building operations generate more than two-thirds of city government-operations emissions, and the city is charged with bringing down emissions to net-zero by 2050.

articles.originalTitle: New Museum Announces 36 Artists and Collectives for 2027 Triennial - ARTnews.com
articles.title: New Museum Announces 36 Artists and Collectives for 2027 Triennial
articles.excerpt: New York's New Museum has announced 36 artists and collectives from 34 countries participating in the sixth Triennial running from February 4 to May 16, 2027.
articles.content: New York's New Museum has announced the 36 artists and collectives participating in the sixth New Museum Triennial, scheduled for February 4 to May 16, 2027. Titled "The Outside Expands," the sixth edition marks the first Triennial to take place at the museum following its recent expansion. According to a museum release, the exhibition is curated by Vivian Crockett and Isabella Rjeille, alongside curatorial assistant Thalia Stefaniuk and curatorial fellow Taeyi Kim, making it the first iteration curated by an international team. The artist roster reflects a wide geographic spread, with 36 participants hailing from 34 countries, marking the institution's broadest international representation to date. The geographic distribution spans Australia, South Africa, India, Mexico, South Korea, Spain, Brazil, and Greece. Only four artists reside in the United States, while Berlin and London are tied with three artists each. The exhibition title draws partial inspiration from a 1979 artist intervention in Brazil. The showcase highlights artists who destabilize fixed notions of territory, identity, gender, and sexuality while fostering alternative collaborations.

articles.originalTitle: Bilbao Fine Arts Museum gains new €45m Norman Foster-designed wing - The Art Newspaper
articles.title: Bilbao Fine Arts Museum Opens New Norman Foster-Designed Wing
articles.excerpt: The Fine Arts Museum in Bilbao, Spain, has opened its new €45m wing designed by architects Norman Foster and Luis María Uriarte. Described as a floating pavilion, the expansion doubles the museum's exhibition space.
articles.content: Located in the industrial port city of Bilbao in Spain's Basque Country, the Fine Arts Museum has opened its new €45m expansion designed by Foster + Partners in collaboration with Luis María Uriarte. Described as a floating pavilion, the striking project doubles the museum's exhibition space to approximately 6,000 sq. m and remodels 8,000 sq. m of existing galleries. The extension connects a 1945 Neo-Classical building and a 1970 Modernist structure, sitting above them with two curved upper storeys held up by giant V-shaped supports. The uppermost floor houses temporary exhibitions, a viewing terrace, a restaurant, and dedicated spaces for architecture and design. Funding for the project came from the Basque government, the regional government, the provincial council, Bilbao city council, and the privately-owned BBK Banking Foundation. Museum director Miguel Zugaza noted that the design respects existing architecture while integrating previous styles. Situated roughly 500 metres from the Guggenheim Museum, the Fine Arts Museum aims to expand its cultural offering as the Basque Country's national gallery.

articles.originalTitle: From an indoor forest to a toilet made with seaweed: Design Museum Gent reopens after €20m eco-focused expansion - The Art Newspaper
articles.title: Design Museum Gent Reopens After Major Expansion
articles.excerpt: Design Museum Gent reopened to the public on October 3 following a four-year expansion and renovation project costing 20 million euros.
articles.content: Design Museum Gent reopened its doors on October 3 following a four-year renovation and expansion project totaling 20 million euros. The undertaking introduced a new five-level wing named DING, which provides approximately 2,000 square meters of flexible space designated for workshops, lectures, and exhibitions. The institution utilized sustainable materials across ten new lavatories, featuring seaweed-derived panels, recycled household plastics, and volcanic ash floor tiles. The facade of the new wing incorporates over 82,000 locally produced Gent Waste Bricks constructed from lime-cured municipal waste. An intervening vacant lot between the museum's historic buildings was transformed into an enclosed atrium serving as the primary entrance and central foyer. Current temporary exhibitions exploring design and democracy alongside public participation will run until April 11, 2027.

articles.originalTitle: Cosima von Bonin’s soft toys storm the Petit Palais - Art Basel
articles.title: Cosima von Bonin’s Soft Sculptures Travel to the Petit Palais
articles.excerpt: German artist Cosima von Bonin presents her "Dollys & Beaux" exhibition at the Petit Palais for Art Basel Paris’s public program.
articles.content: Kenyan-born German artist Cosima von Bonin is presenting her exhibition titled "Dollys & Beaux" at the Petit Palais as part of Art Basel Paris's public program. The exhibition features large-scale textile sculptures crafted from leather, velvet, and mohair. These oversized creature sculptures previously appeared in Loewe's Fall/Winter 2026 fashion show, where the artist's imagery also influenced garments and accessories. The display includes midnight-blue velvet St. Bernard dog sculptures with plush barrels, sea scallops, an octopus, and a killer whale. Throughout her career, von Bonin has maintained a playful resistance to artistic hierarchies, deliberately leaving room for viewers to form their own interpretations without rigid authorial direction. Her works often use oversized stuffed animals as antiheroes that challenge contemporary pressures of productivity and speed through a lens of humor and withdrawal. The "Dollys & Beaux" exhibition will be on view at the Petit Palais from October 23 to 25, 2026.

articles.originalTitle: Wasl Tower / UNS - ArchDaily
articles.title: The 302-Metre Wasl Tower Completed in Dubai
articles.excerpt: Built in downtown Dubai, the 302-metre mixed-use Wasl Tower brings together hotel, residential, office, and public spaces within a single vertical community.
articles.content: Rising in downtown Dubai near Sheikh Zayed Road and the Burj Khalifa, Wasl Tower stands as a 302-metre mixed-use high-rise designed by UNS in collaboration with lead engineering consultant Werner Sobek for Wasl Group. Spanning an area of 167733 square metres, the tower integrates hotel, residential, office, and public amenity spaces into a single vertical community, contributing a distinctive presence to Dubai's city centre. The project involved contributions from numerous design, engineering, and specialist consultants. Hotel interiors were designed by GA Design, while food and beverage interior spaces were handled by LWD. Facade lighting design was executed by Arup, with landscape architecture led by Green4Cities Architects and Terra Firma Landscape. Local MEP engineering was provided by SEED, and quantity surveying services were managed by Kulkarni Quantity Surveyors. The high-rise structure adds a new multi-functional architectural landmark to the urban landscape of the United Arab Emirates.

articles.originalTitle: Dive into Guadalajara modernism: a lesser-known strand of Mexican architecture - wallpaper.com
articles.title: Guadalajara Modernism: A Lesser-Known Strand of Mexican Architecture
articles.excerpt: The capital of Mexico's Jalisco State emerged as a prominent hub for experimental 20th-century architecture, blending international modernist currents with local vernacular traditions through figures like Luis Barragán and Pedro Castellanos Lambley.
articles.content: Guadalajara served as a prominent playground for experimental 20th-century architecture in Mexico. During the 1920s and 1930s, Luis Barragán, Ignacio Díaz Morales, Pedro Castellanos Lambley, and Rafael Urzúa established the Tapatía Architecture School, embracing a contextual approach that linked modern influences with Jalisco State's vernacular traditions. Born in the city, Barragán settled back after European travels to design numerous private homes in the Colonia Americana district, drawing on colonial traditions, Art Deco, and colour. By 1934, he designed a stark white home and studio for painter José Clemente Orozco, shifting toward avant-garde functionalism. Simultaneously, Pedro Castellanos Lambley designed Casa Quiñones in 1930, considered the city's first modernist house, blending international Art Deco with a regional twist. Cultural integration also materialized through José Clemente Orozco's 57 murals inside the UNESCO World Heritage site Hospicio Cabañas. In 1948, ITESO established an architecture department rooted in Bauhaus ideas, inviting figures such as Mathias Goeritz to teach. Following World War II, rapid urban development fostered brutalist and modernist structures by architects such as Félix Aceves Ortega, who utilized primary geometric shapes, and Alejandro Zohn Rosenthal, who realized the Mercado Libertad.

articles.originalTitle: On World Architecture Day 2026: A Call to Build Better, Build Differently, and Share Resources - ArchDaily
articles.title: International Union of Architects Issues Call for Housing Crisis on World Architecture Day
articles.excerpt: Marking World Architecture Day, the International Union of Architects drew attention to housing as a human right, calling on architects to contribute to equitable access.
articles.content: Designated by the International Union of Architects on the first Monday of October in alignment with the United Nations World Habitat Day, World Architecture Day draws attention to the global housing crisis as a fundamental element of human dignity and well-being. Under the motto "Housing is a Human Right. Build It," the organization calls on architects to advance equitable access to housing through design, research, and advocacy. According to United Nations data, more than 3 billion people lack access to adequate housing, over 1.1 billion live in informal settlements, and hundreds of millions experience unrecorded homelessness. The crisis consists of multiple interconnected barriers requiring not only new residential construction, but building better, sharing more resources, and fully utilizing existing structures. Uniting professional organizations from more than 120 countries and territories, the global non-governmental federation stresses that housing must never be treated as a luxury asset. On World Architecture Day, the organization invites architects worldwide to promote creative strategies addressing housing demand through lectures, exhibitions, webinars, and public outreach initiatives.

articles.originalTitle: Yohji Yamamoto Drawings - Victoria and Albert Museum
articles.title: Victoria and Albert Museum Hosts Talk on Unpublished Yohji Yamamoto Drawings
articles.excerpt: The Victoria and Albert Museum will host an event celebrating a collection of previously unpublished drawings by designer Yohji Yamamoto.
articles.content: The Victoria and Albert Museum is hosting a special talk and book celebration on Wednesday 9 December to mark the publication of Yohji Yamamoto Drawings. Author and curator Alexandre Samson will join Yohji Yamamoto's executive advisor, Caroline Fabre, at V&A South Kensington to discuss a collection of never-before-published drawings selected by Yamamoto himself. Featuring menswear and womenswear sketches designed with support from Peter Saville, the book offers insight into the designer's creative process and his exploration of fashion and form. Samson and Fabre will discuss Yamamoto's creative practice and the enduring legacy of his work during the evening event, which includes a wine reception and book signing. Priority booking for members is open, with general ticket sales beginning on 19 October, subject to availability. Ticket prices range from 15.00 to 20.00 pounds and include the post-talk reception.

articles.originalTitle: Painting large as an Impressionist: Renoir and the full-length format | Events - The National Gallery, London
articles.title: National Gallery Examines Renoir and Full-Length Portraiture
articles.excerpt: Colin B. Bailey, Director of The Morgan Library and Museum, will deliver a special lecture at the National Gallery's Pigott Theatre exploring Pierre-Auguste Renoir's large-scale portraits.
articles.content: The National Gallery is hosting a special event focusing on Pierre-Auguste Renoir's full-length portraits, recognized among the most ambitious works of his career. Held in conjunction with the exhibition Renoir and Love, the lecture features Colin B. Bailey, Katharine J. Rayner Director of The Morgan Library & Museum, who will examine how the artist captured modern life, emotions, and social interactions in 19th-century Paris. Drawing on decades of research into eighteenth- and nineteenth-century French art, Bailey will explore Renoir's technical brilliance, evolving portraiture approach, and psychological immediacy. The talk will take place in the Pigott Theatre on Level -1 of the Sainsbury Wing. Standard tickets are priced at 10 pounds, while concessions are available at 8 pounds for full-time students, jobseekers, and disabled adults. Advance booking is required for attendance, and members will have the option to join the event online. This lecture offers audiences a distinct opportunity to closely examine the artist's celebrated figures within the broader context of friendship, love, and modernity explored throughout the exhibition.

articles.originalTitle: Renoir and Love | Exhibitions - The National Gallery, London
articles.title: National Gallery in London Opens Major Renoir and Love Exhibition
articles.excerpt: The National Gallery in London presents Renoir and Love, an exhibition exploring the artist's depiction of human connections and everyday emotions through 40 paintings gathered from international collections, on view until January 31, 2027.
articles.content: The National Gallery in London presents Renoir and Love, an exhibition focusing on Pierre-Auguste Renoir's exploration of love, friendship, and human connection during his peak period from the 1860s to the 1880s. Running until January 31, 2027, the exhibition brings together 40 paintings from collections across the world, highlighting the artist's role as an innovator of Impressionism. Notably, Renoir's iconic 1876 painting Bal au Moulin de la Galette from the Musée d'Orsay is on display in the United Kingdom for the first time. The exhibition is organized jointly by the Musée d'Orsay, the National Gallery, and the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston. Visitors can explore sun-dappled gardens, dance halls, and intimate everyday moments captured by the artist, with flexible pay-what-you-wish admission options available on select Friday evenings.

articles.originalTitle: Roy Lichtenstein: Like New | Museum Exhibitions | News - Gagosian
articles.title: Roy Lichtenstein Retrospective Opens at Whitney Museum in New York
articles.excerpt: The Whitney Museum of American Art presents Roy Lichtenstein: Like New, marking the artist's first retrospective in New York since 1993 and gathering roughly 130 works created from the early 1940s through the 1990s.
articles.content: The Whitney Museum of American Art in New York hosts Roy Lichtenstein: Like New from October 11, 2026, to May 10, 2027. Marking the artist's first major retrospective in the city since 1993, the exhibition traces how Lichtenstein's early interest in perception and visual recognition shaped a career-long investigation into duplication, simulation, and image culture. Featuring approximately 130 works produced from the early 1940s to the 1990s, the exhibition explores his treatment of images as unstable forms subject to borrowing, translation, and reframing. For the first time, all works from Lichtenstein's inaugural Pop-style exhibition at the Leo Castelli Gallery in 1962 are reunited. This pivotal moment defined an era and extended its impact beyond Pop art, shaping subsequent generations of artists whose works are also displayed within the exhibition.

articles.originalTitle: Patek Philippe Unveils Seventh Watch Art Grand Exhibition in Milan, Debuts Limited-edition Timepieces - WWD
articles.title: Patek Philippe Unveils Seventh Watch Art Grand Exhibition in Milan
articles.excerpt: Swiss watchmaker Patek Philippe has launched its seventh Watch Art Grand Exhibition in Milan, showcasing historical timepieces and debuting new limited-edition models.
articles.content: Swiss watchmaker Patek Philippe has opened its seventh Watch Art Grand Exhibition at CityOval Milano, marking the largest edition of the event to date. Spanning fifteen thematic rooms, the exhibition features contemporary collections alongside historical timepieces from museum archives and items predating the firm's founding. Artisans are also demonstrating traditional decorative techniques such as enameling, guillochage, and gem-setting within a dedicated space. To mark the occasion, the manufacturer debuted seven new limited-edition references featuring sapphire crystal casebacks inscribed with Milano 2026, including three Calatrava models representing the Italian flag and world-time pieces depicting downtown Milan. The showcase also introduced the Gondolo Ladies First jewelry watch collection. Running through October 18, the Milan exhibition follows previous iterations held in cities such as Munich, London, New York, Singapore, Tokyo, and Dubai.

articles.excerpt: Swiss watchmaker Patek Philippe has launched its largest Watch Art Grand Exhibition to date at CityOval Milano, featuring over 500 timepieces alongside exclusive limited-edition models created specifically for the Italian market.

articles.originalTitle: New Work: The Long Goodbye by Carrie Mae Weems - Victoria and Albert Museum
articles.title: Carrie Mae Weems Explores Migration and History in New Work at V&A East Museum
articles.excerpt: Commissioned for the opening of V&A East Museum, Carrie Mae Weems's The Long Goodbye explores migration through love stories intertwined within human journeys.
articles.content: Commissioned for the opening of V&A East Museum and developed over nearly three years, The Long Goodbye examines migration through the obscured love stories intertwined within human journeys. The project seeks to restore humanity to individuals whose courage and labor shaped the modern world but whose lives are frequently reduced to statistics or omitted from historical accounts. This commission turns Weems's lens toward the UK and its diasporic communities for the first time. Over the course of its development, Weems's initial ideas evolved in response to migration debates and protests prominent in the political climates of both Britain and the United States. The film imagines a different account of post-war Britain, recognizing the buried truths regarding how and why generations immigrated to the UK. Water functions centrally as a route of migration, a connector between geographies, and a vessel of history. Drawing on the concept of tidalectics developed by Barbadian poet and historian Kamu Brathwaite, the imagery understands history through the ebb and flow of tides. The work is exhibited alongside two archival films, Before the Loss of You and Okwui.

articles.originalTitle: A Metal-Clad Mass-Timber Building by Lever Architecture Unites Portland State University’s Art and Design School - Architectural Record
articles.title: Portland State University art and design school unites in new building
articles.excerpt: Designed by Lever Architecture, the 4-story Jordan Schnitzer building unites three previously dispersed art and design departments at Portland State University under a single roof for the first time.
articles.content: Opening at Portland State University, the four-story, roughly 107,000-square-foot Jordan Schnitzer School of Art + Art History + Design unites three major departments previously dispersed across campus under a single roof. Described by Lever Architecture founding principal Thomas Robinson as cultural infrastructure terminating the city's South Park Blocks, the structure rises from a former parking lot and skate park site. Wrapped in custom-formed green metal panels evoking a forest canopy, the building utilizes cross-laminated timber floor panels and a glulam column-and-beam system, bolstering the region's mass-timber industry. More than half of the Douglas fir glulam used was sourced from tribally owned forests and certified mills across the Pacific Northwest. The building features a central commons area, interconnected exhibition galleries, an open-air courtyard, and studios designed to connect students with the dense urban setting. Brightly colored steel fire stairs and sustainable wood materials complement the architectural design of the facility.

articles.originalTitle: White-brick extension defines Design Museum Gent revamp - Dezeen
articles.title: Design Museum Gent Expands With Waste-Based White Brick Extension
articles.excerpt: Design Museum Gent in Belgium has been revamped and expanded using waste-based white bricks by studios Carmody Groarke, Atama, and Re-st.
articles.content: Design Museum Gent in Belgium has undergone a major revamp led by architecture studios Carmody Groarke, Atama, and Re-st. The project involved restoring three historic wings, renovating an existing courtyard, and adding a timber-framed extension. Spanning a total of 8,600 square metres, the expansion makes the venue Belgium's largest design museum. The extension features a facade of white bricks produced from local construction waste through a low-energy lime-curing process. Developed alongside specialist partners, these bricks are reported to carry one-third of the embodied carbon found in typical Belgian clay bricks. Rising six storeys, the new wing accommodates ground-floor exhibition spaces, lecture and education areas, and a top-level event venue overlooking the city. The building also incorporates a 3D-printed aluminium entrance door by Unfold and works by various local creatives. The museum reopens to the public featuring new collections.

articles.originalTitle: Biennale Arte 2026 | India Pavilion: Seeds of the Sacred - A Bharatanatyam Offering to the Human Spirit - labiennale.org
articles.title: India Pavilion Presents Bharatanatyam Performance at Biennale Arte 2026
articles.excerpt: As part of Biennale Arte 2026, the India Pavilion hosts a traditional Bharatanatyam performance titled Seeds of the Sacred by Anwesha Das.
articles.content: The India Pavilion within the framework of Biennale Arte 2026 presents a special event inviting audiences to explore the strength of the human spirit. Hosted at the Teatro Piccolo Arsenale, the performance titled Seeds of the Sacred - A Bharatanatyam Offering to the Human Spirit is performed by artist Anwesha Das. As one of India's oldest classical dance forms, Bharatanatyam integrates movement, expression, music, and storytelling deeply rooted in tradition. Inspired by the themes of In Minor Keys, this presentation explores authenticity, humility, earth-rootedness, and spiritual proportion. The performance seeks to reconnect audiences with nature and essential human dimensions through bodily movement and gesture. Admission to the event requires a reservation, with the programme scheduled from 19:00 to 20:00.

articles.originalTitle: TfL reveals civil engineering behind £15.3M step-free upgrades at Surrey Quays and Northolt - New Civil Engineer
articles.title: Surrey Quays and Northolt Stations Gain Step-Free Access
articles.excerpt: London stations Surrey Quays and Northolt now offer step-free access for wheelchair users and passengers with pushchairs, following recent civil engineering upgrades.
articles.content: Surrey Quays and Northolt railway stations in London now feature step-free access to accommodate wheelchair users and travelers with luggage or pushchairs. According to Transport for London, the Surrey Quays project introduced a new entrance, ticket hall, accessible toilets, and two new lifts serving both platforms. Funded largely through an 80.8 million pound package from the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government, construction began in January 2026 and concluded in September 2026. At Northolt station on the Central line, a new footbridge and lift were installed to connect the street and trains directly. Costing an estimated 15.3 million pounds, the Northolt project ran from February 2025 to September 2026, making it the ninety-fifth station on the Tube network to achieve step-free access. Officials noted that these infrastructure upgrades will significantly improve travel options and journey feasibility for elderly residents, disabled individuals, and parents across the transport network.

articles.originalTitle: Advancement in Shallow Foundations - American Society of Civil Engineers (ASCE)
articles.title: Advancements in Shallow Foundations and Ground Improvement in Geotechnical Engineering
articles.excerpt: The Geo-Institute Shallow Foundations Technical Committee will examine ground improvement methods, fill materials on complex sites, modulus of subgrade reaction, and recycled plastic pins in soil stabilization.
articles.content: Current technical approaches regarding shallow foundations and ground improvement technologies continue to be discussed in geotechnical engineering. Although shallow foundations are widely preferred for their cost advantages and simplicity, ground improvement techniques may be required in fill or weak soil conditions. In this context, the significance of scale effects in determining the modulus of subgrade reaction and analyzing foundation-soil interaction is emphasized. Evaluations indicate that values obtained from plate load tests can differ from behaviors observed in large foundation analyses. Furthermore, innovative material solutions, such as lightweight cellular concrete, can resolve stability issues in complex sites containing waste materials. In military and civil infrastructure applications, the use of recycled plastic pins is examined to stabilize weak subgrades. Finite element analyses demonstrate that these pins, when placed at appropriate spacings, can reduce vertical displacements and support foundation systems.

articles.originalTitle: Chanel Brings Le19M Closer to Chinese Art World, Local Craft With Pudong Art Exhibition - WWD
articles.title: Chanel Brings La Galerie Du 19M Exhibition to Pudong Art Museum
articles.excerpt: The Pudong Art Museum in Shanghai hosts its largest exhibition format, bringing together French and Chinese artisans and artists.
articles.content: Seeking to deepen its relationship with Asia, the fashion house opened the latest edition of its project at the Pudong Art Museum on the Huangpu River. Taking over the entire third floor, the free exhibition is its largest format to date and the brand's biggest local project of the year. Following iterations in Dakar and Tokyo, the project brings together ateliers such as Lesage, Montex, Goossens and Lognon alongside more than 31 creative guests from China and France. Arriving amid renewed consumer interest in handicrafts, the exhibition introduces the identity of the brand's Métiers d'Art hub to a local audience. Bruno Pavlovsky stated that the exhibition focuses on the intangible creative process rather than the final products. Curated by Gong Yan, Lin Tianmiao, Zhang Lei and Christelle Kocher, the event highlights sustainability through the upcycling of discarded materials into artworks. Featuring works by artists including Yin Xiuzhen, Ding Yi and Lin Tianmiao, the exhibition will run until November 15.
